posts.text: ❗️ At the time of the pandemic, Boikov had shot to infamy as a vocal opposition to Covid-19 vaccines and restrictions. Online, he was testing the long arm of the law by hosting “freedom” protests and vlogging defiant showdowns with police. “They hated me, I was making a laughing-stock of them and they could never get me,” he says. Behind the scenes, however, Mr Boikov says he had been working with police on a different cause: exposing a notorious pedophile priest. He says he knew multiple victims of Alexis Rosentool, and started encouraging them to make statements in the hope of bringing the priest to justice. “He’d got away with it for many years,” Mr Boikov said. “I started the whole process.” Mr Boikov eventually became disillusioned with the investigation and decided to use his platform at freedom rallies to publicly name Mr Rosentool. Mr Rosentool was later jailed for 19 years over multiple child abuse charges. Mr Boikov, meanwhile, was imprisoned in 2022 for breaching the suppression order. “I don’t regret it. After that, many more victims came forward.” He was shackled and sent to a maximum-security prison alongside terrorists, murderers and members of the notorious Alameddine clan. Mr Boikov was “shocked” to be classified as an extreme high risk inmate, which he believes is the strictest ever punishment in Australia for breaching a suppression order. But thanks to his anti-authoritarian content, he had no trouble with his new neighbours. What wore him down, in fact, was the loss of phone access to keep up his online crusade. “The only phone I could use belonged to one of the Alemadines. He was a nice guy,” he says. After walking free on bail after serving four months, Mr Boikov made up his mind: it was time to replant his roots in Russia. But shopping in Sydney CBD one day, he fatefully stumbled on a pro-Ukraine protest, during which a man fell and was injured. That’s when Mr Boikov fled to the consulate. ❗️ Mr Boikov’s supporters argue that his role in bringing Rosentool to justice, together with the years he has spent inside the consulate, should count in his favour. But the Australian authorities have given little indication they’re prepared to let him walk from the outstanding charges. “Australia remains deeply concerned about Russia’s use of disinformation globally, including efforts to justify its illegal and immoral invasion of Ukraine,” said a spokesperson for the Department of Foreign Affairs. “The Australian Government’s position is that Mr Boikov must face the criminal charges against him.” A NSW police spokesperson confirmed they “continue to seek the arrest of a 36-year-old man currently wanted on two outstanding warrants”. Meanwhile, the DFAT spokesperson notes consulates are “inviolable’’ under international law – meaning the host country has no right to enter them without permission. “Any law enforcement actions in relation to Mr Boikov are a matter for NSW Police.” Ukrainian ambassador Vasyl Myroshnychenko, who is no stranger to Russian propaganda, echoed the warning for vigilance. “Australians should be alert to Russian propaganda operations,” he says. “Russia has specific strategies for trying to undermine Australia’s social fabric.” Full story : https://www.news.com.au/national/aussie-cossack-simeon-boikov-joins-russian-political-party-from-inside-sydney-consulate/news-story/30cf23ffdabe24c521e01918dd5d0319

Сегодня годовщина начала Майдана, а накануне этого дня, 20 ноября 2013 я с трибуны Верховной Рады обвинил посольство США в подготовке переворота на Украине. Националисты орали так, что я себя не слышал. Слава Богу, микрофон чувствительнее, чем мои уши, иначе разобрать, что я говорю, было бы невозможно. Мое выступление длилось столько, сколько было отведено для выступления руководителя фракции. С формальной точки зрения я, как заместитель руководителя фракции, имел право так делать. Но фактически мое выступление не было согласовано с руководством фракции и Партии и было моей личной инициативой. Когда я сошёл с трибуны, мне навстречу устремилась возмущённая Анна Герман со словами, что я не имею полномочий обвинять Соединённые Штаты. Выручил меня Михаил Чечетов, который обогнал Герман, бросился ко мне навстречу, обнял, оттеснил Герман: «Наконец хоть кто-то назвал вещи своими именами!» После выступления я уехал к себе в Днепропетровск и вернулся в Киев по просьбе руководителей Партии уже в разгар Майдана.

❗️ Dr Robert Horvath, a specialist in Russian politics at La Trobe University, says the party maintains a thin veneer of autonomy within a political system dominated by the Russian president. “The party operates within a system completely controlled by the Kremlin,” he says. “It’s historically very close with Russian security, intelligence and security structures.” Despite its label as an opposition party, the LDPR is widely characterised by political scholars as serving the Kremlin. It has spent decades in the State Duma and is no fringe outfit operating on the edges of Russian politics. Mr Boikov’s recruitment, Dr Horvath says, could demonstrate the Kremlin’s appetite for fresh voices capable of projecting Russian influence abroad. Dr Horvath says his recruitment could hold significant implications for Australia. “Mr Boikov is very well-connected in far-right circles, so accepting an institutionalised role in Russia could be potentially significant for Australia,” he says. “His principal value to the Russian state is as a propagandist who can mobilise, disrupt and destabilise Western democracy.” That’s Mr Boikov’s secret weapon: the power to present Russian messaging to the West. “As an experienced propagandist with an Australian accent, he has an authentic charm,” Dr Horvath admits. ❗️ Mr Boikov, who welcomed a son with his glamorous wife in December last year, likens life in the consulate to being “suspended in space”. Inside, he sleeps in a makeshift bedroom, does callisthenics to maintain fitness and spends his days pumping out pro-Russian content – often without direct sunlight. In 2023, this content landed him on the Australian government’s foreign influence transparency register. The irony is not lost on him: in crusading against Covid lockdowns, he landed in a lockdown of his own making. ❗️ Mr Kramar denied LDPR is encouraging Mr Boikov to renounce his Australian citizenship, and insists the party was only “extending a helping hand”. It’s a remarkable rise to power for Mr Boikov, whose highest rank until now has been as a propagandist employed by Russian state-run media. What remains unclear is what responsibilities the opportunity will involve, and the influence Mr Boikov’s membership could play in a handover deal. What’s no secret is the power Mr Boikov holds for the regime. “His experience and first-hand insight into the inner workings of the West are invaluable assets,” Mr Kramar said. “But, above all, he has remained, at his core, a Russian.” So how, living inside a tiny room in his de facto residence, does a Sydney influencer become qualified for Russian politics? ❗️ In a bombshell statement to news.com.au , LDPR Supreme Council Member Andrey Kramar confirmed Mr Boikov will soon be a card-carrying member of the party. Mr Kramar, who has a seat in the Russian occupied Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) region of eastern Ukraine, used Mr Boikov’s plight as a defiant message for the West. “Let me state this firmly, for the whole world to hear: Russians do not abandon their own.” The move marks an extraordinary twist in the story of the notorious nationalist, who has spent years offering himself as part of a potential prisoner exchange deal with Moscow. But can Mr Putin’s man Down Under really trade his Sydney hide-out for a seat at Moscow’s political table? ❗️ An infamous Aussie fugitive has accepted a world-first offer to reinvent himself as a Russian politician, news.com.au can reveal. Simeon Boikov, known online as the Aussie Cossack, has spent almost four years dodging arrest warrants within the walls of Sydney’s Russian Consulates. News.com.au has confirmed Mr Boikov has joined the Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR). Despite its name, LDPR is known for extreme, ultranationalist politics that back President Putin’s war in Ukraine. From his self-imposed exile, the pro-Putin podcaster is accused of being a serial pest who haunts the Albanese government meddling in Aussie politics. But now, the man dubbed “Russia’s Julian Assange” appears to have mapped an extraordinary exit route: through the machinery of Mr Putin’s power. While in hiding, Mr Putin has already granted Mr Boikov citizenship. And while diplomatic asylum seekers are not new, news.com.au understands this is the only known case of someone holed up in a consulate accepting a government post.
